title: MCP close_ticket/update_ticket_status reject Rick himself with capability-token error
source_context: Closing RICK-027/RICK-029 after sprint review in rick-terminal project, 2026-07-03
description: From a Rick session in another project (rick-terminal), mcp__cto-orchestrator__create_ticket and delegate work fine, but close_ticket and update_ticket_status return 'unauthorized: missing or invalid agent capability token'. Rick (the orchestrating session) has no capability token — those tools seem to expect a delegated-Morty token. Either exempt the orchestrator session or document that Rick must use ticket.py close as fallback.
proposed_changes: Check the capability-token middleware on write tools in the MCP server: create_ticket is unguarded while close_ticket/update_ticket_status are guarded — make it consistent and allow the interactive Rick session.
reject_reason: Triage reject-invalid: target_files is empty, which per verification rules is an automatic reject-invalid — nothing concrete to delegate. Note: the underlying bug is NOT stale; it is still present in scripts/mcp_server.py (create_ticket unguarded, update_ticket_status/close_ticket guarded by _require_agent_token with no orchestrator exemption in verify_agent_token).
